name: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? (MAST)
authors: Mert Cemri, Melissa Z. Pan, Shuyi Yang, et al. (13 authors incl. Dan Klein, Matei Zaharia, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Ion Stoica); lead affiliation UC Berkeley (with Intesa Sanpaolo).
venue: NeurIPS 2025 (poster); originally arXiv preprint (arXiv:2503.13657, submitted Mar 2025, last revised v3 Oct 2025).
code_url: Open-sourced: MAST-Data traces/annotations + LLM-as-a-Judge annotator released; MAST usable as a Python library via `pip install agentdash` (GitHub: multi-agent-systems-failure-taxonomy / mast-related repos by the authors).
reflection_type: none — this is a failure-analysis/diagnosis work, not a self-correction method. It builds an empirical failure taxonomy (MAST) and an LLM-as-a-Judge annotator; reflection/correction is the object of study, not a mechanism the paper proposes. (One studied failure mode, FM-2.6 / superficial self-reflection-style errors, concerns reasoning-action mismatch in agents.)
feedback_source: human (expert annotators with kappa=0.88 inter-annotator agreement) for taxonomy construction; LLM-as-a-Judge (GPT-4o-based) for scalable annotation, validated against human ground-truth labels. Diagnostic interventions use task-success-rate (environment/oracle) signals.
iteration_structure: single-shot (analysis/taxonomy work). Methodology iterates over traces via Grounded Theory open-coding rounds, but the artifact is a static taxonomy + dataset + judge, not an iterative agent loop.
reflection_object: n/a as a self-improvement target. As an object of analysis, MAST characterizes failures in the agents' action trajectory, inter-agent communication/coordination, system design/prompt specification, and verification stages of multi-agent LLM systems.
learning_locus: n/a (failure-analysis / dataset / taxonomy work; no learning signal or weight update in the contribution itself).
requires_training: none for the core contribution (taxonomy + dataset + LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline use prompting/in-context judging). Diagnostic interventions are prompt/workflow edits, not training.
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge / meta-judge in the analysis sense: an LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline annotates failure modes (94% accuracy, Cohen's kappa 0.77 vs human experts). No trained reward model; ground-truth comes from human annotation.
distillation_target: none — the reusable artifacts are the MAST taxonomy, the MAST-Data trace dataset, and the LLM annotator, not a distilled reflection/skill/weights. (Closest analogue: a structured rules/taxonomy framework for diagnosing failures.)
emergent_vs_engineered: n/a — the paper does not propose reflective behavior. The failures it catalogs arise in scaffold-engineered MAS (e.g., ChatDev, MetaGPT, AG2); one insight is that some failures (e.g., inter-agent misalignment / 'theory of mind' collapse) are not fixable by scaffolding alone and may require model-level training.
memory_type: none (analysis work). The released MAST-Data is a static annotated-trace corpus, not an agent memory module.
memory_persistence: n/a (no agent memory mechanism proposed; MAST-Data is a persistent released dataset/resource).
memory_curation_mechanism: n/a — no memory curation mechanism. Dataset curation used Grounded Theory open coding over traces and theoretical sampling, but this is research methodology, not runtime memory curation.
error_localization_granularity: agent-level (multi-agent) and step-level: MAST attributes failures to specific failure modes occurring at specific stages/agents within a trace (e.g., a particular agent disobeying role spec, a step repetition, a verification step). The taxonomy spans holistic system-design issues down to step-level coordination/verification errors.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: n/a as a learning method. As analysis, it studies failures within individual task traces across many tasks/benchmarks to extract generalizable failure modes.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: n/a — diagnostic, not corrective at runtime. The paper's MAST-guided interventions are post-hoc system-design fixes (e.g., adding a verification step, fixing role specification) applied between runs, i.e., closer to post-hoc-revision / avoidance via redesign rather than mid-trajectory recovery.
task_domains: code (software development), math, general agent / tool-use & web tasks (general agentic problem-solving). Spans coding, math problem-solving, and general agent benchmarks.
benchmarks: ProgramDev / ProgramDev-v2 (ChatDev, MetaGPT, OpenManus), SWE-Bench Lite (HyperAgent), AppWorld Test-C, GSM-Plus / GSMPlus (AG2 MathChat), OlympiadBench, MMLU, GAIA (Magentic-One). 7 MAS frameworks: ChatDev, MetaGPT, HyperAgent, AppWorld, AG2 (MathChat), Magentic-One, OpenManus.
headline_result: Built MAST: 14 fine-grained failure modes in 3 categories (System Design, Inter-Agent Misalignment, Task Verification) from analysis of 150 traces with kappa=0.88 inter-annotator agreement; MAST-Data = 1600+ annotated traces across 7 MAS frameworks and 4 model families; LLM-as-a-Judge annotator reaches 94% accuracy / Cohen's kappa 0.77 vs human experts. MAST-guided interventions yield up to +15.6% task-success improvement (e.g., adding a high-level objective-verification step to ChatDev on ProgramDev; +9.4% from fixing CEO role specification) with the same underlying LLM.
baselines: Not a method-vs-baseline paper. Comparisons are: human annotation vs LLM-as-a-Judge annotation (agreement); and baseline (unmodified) MAS configurations vs MAST-guided intervention variants. Contrasted conceptually with prior work like the Who&When dataset (Zhang et al.) for failure attribution.
gains_vs_baseline: Intervention case studies on the SAME base LLM: +9.4% overall task success (ChatDev, ensuring the CEO/leader agent has final say / improved role specification), and a maximum +15.6% improvement (ChatDev on ProgramDev, adding a high-level task-objective verification step). The paper stresses these isolated fixes are insufficient and full reliability needs structural MAS redesign.
compute_cost_profile: Annotation cost: LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline replaces expensive human annotation (humans spent many hours per disagreement-resolution round). No inference-multiplier claim for a proposed agent method (there is none). Interventions add an extra verification/role step (modest extra agent calls) but no training cost.
known_limitations: Failures often stem from fundamental system-design and model-level limitations (e.g., 'theory of mind' / social-reasoning gaps in inter-agent misalignment) that scaffolding fixes (e.g., MCP/A2A communication protocols, prompt tweaks) cannot fully resolve; MAST-guided fixes give partial gains only. Failure distributions are illustrative and depend on specific MAS/benchmark/model configurations; LLM-as-a-Judge agreement (kappa 0.77) is lower than human IAA (0.88). Taxonomy/dataset are descriptive, not a solution.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: For diagnosis: relies on human expert labels (oracle ground-truth) to build/validate the taxonomy and the LLM judge. For intervention evaluation: env-reward / task-success-rate (and human-evaluated completion). The LLM-as-a-Judge itself performs intrinsic LLM judgment validated against oracle labels.
self_correction_efficacy: task-dependent (and a cautionary finding). The paper documents that current MAS self-verification and inter-agent self-correction are often inadequate (FC3 task-verification failures; FM-3.2 no/incomplete verification, FM-3.3 incorrect verification), and that agents frequently fail to detect/correct their own errors; multi-level verification is needed rather than sole reliance on final-stage low-level checks.
calibration_effect: not-measured (no calibration / confidence study; out of scope).
failure_attribution_capability: classifies-failure-mode (taxonomy) AND attributes-responsible-agent / attributes-failing-step: MAST is a 14-mode/3-category taxonomy and the annotation pipeline localizes which failure mode occurs (often tied to a specific agent and stage) within a trace.
failure_mode_addressed: Defines/exposes 14 failure modes in 3 categories. FC1 System Design: FM-1.1 disobey task specification (11.8%), FM-1.2 disobey role specification (1.5%), FM-1.3 step repetition (15.7%), FM-1.4 loss of conversation history / context loss (2.8%), FM-1.5 unaware of termination conditions / not recognizing completion (12.4%). FC2 Inter-Agent Misalignment: FM-2.1 conversation reset (2.2%), FM-2.2 fail to ask for clarification / proceed on wrong assumptions (6.8%), FM-2.3 task derailment (7.4%), FM-2.4 information withholding (0.85%), FM-2.5 ignored other agent's input (1.9%), FM-2.6 reasoning-action mismatch (13.2%). FC3 Task Verification: FM-3.1 premature termination (6.2%), FM-3.2 no or incomplete verification (8.2%), FM-3.3 incorrect verification (9.1%). Cross-links to MAST's own canonical 14 modes (this paper IS MAST); relevant to inter-agent misalignment, premature termination, superficial verification/self-reflection, and error-loop (step repetition) modes.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: Yes — MAST-Data: 1600+ annotated traces across 7 MAS frameworks and 4 model families (GPT-4/GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.7-Sonnet, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B, CodeLlama-7B); plus MAST-Data-human (inter-annotator study with human labels); the MAST taxonomy itself; and the open-sourced LLM-as-a-Judge annotator pipeline (Python library `agentdash`).
builds_on: Grounded Theory / open-coding qualitative methodology (Glaser & Strauss; Khandkar); prior MAS frameworks it analyzes (ChatDev, MetaGPT, AG2/AutoGen MathChat, HyperAgent, AppWorld, Magentic-One, OpenManus); LLM-as-a-Judge paradigm; concurrent failure-attribution work (Zhang et al. 'Which Agent Causes Task Failures and When?' / Who&When dataset).
extended_by_or_inspired: Widely cited as the anchor MAS-failure taxonomy. Follow-ups include AgenTracer (Who Is Inducing Failure...), FAMAS (spectrum-based failure attribution), CORRECT (condensed error recognition / knowledge transfer), DoVer (intervention-driven auto debugging), Aegis (automated error generation & attribution), AgentAsk (edge-level error taxonomy + clarification module), SupervisorAgent (runtime supervision), and various MAS-reliability/uncertainty works (e.g., Entropy Judger, HiddenBench collective-reasoning failures).
on_policy_distillation_link: Not applicable — no distillation/skill-optimization mechanism. Relevant to OPD-style synthesis only indirectly: the paper argues some failures need model-level training (e.g., for inter-agent 'social reasoning'), motivating training-based rather than purely in-context fixes.
sample_efficiency: n/a (no iterative trial-to-gain metric). Taxonomy was developed from ~150 traces; full MAST-Data spans 1600+ traces.
